page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 1843 GB local SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks place the D48ds_v4 in the average tier for most compute and memory operations, though it exhibits strong memory performance in specific tests. The Passmark memory score is rated as strong, supported by a read-only small-block cached memory bandwidth of 2495.44 GB/sec and a large-block uncached write bandwidth of 47.81 GB/sec. Multi-core processing capabilities are demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 44208.53 and a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression speed of 61.81 GB/sec. However, text generation benchmarks for large language models show weaker performance, with a 7B model achieving 7.75 tokens/sec and a 135M model reaching 50.02 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D48ds_v4 offers a balanced resource density, combining substantial compute power with a large local SSD without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring a mix of CPU capacity and fast local storage. Recommended workloads include relational databases, static web serving, Redis deployments, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
